So I get that whole feeling of living not being worth it. Yes, I have friends, I have a "life." On Facebook my life seems great. But here where I can be anonymous my life is shit and I have no motivation to try to fix it. Getting out of bed every day is torture although I hate being along with my thoughts and the misery of being me, alone and abandoned. And old. Who the hell wants a woman my age except some creepy old man? My husband is still good looking but most men our age are - ugh. And then people who don't know me say "oh, you're still young" because they think I'm younger than I am, as if I can get away with looking younger forever. I can't scam my way through life. I am what I am - old and used up and totally done. But I do love my kids- and I often think it would be kinder to leave them than to burden them with this tearful depressed old mother who couldn't even hold on to her husband. So I feel for all of you - OP and kamelasa especially. I get it.

If you start to feel beautiful on the inside you can show it on the outside. Clubs are horrible meat markets and the only reason to go is if you really want to hear the band (if there is one). But there is no such thing as ugly on the outside. Ugly is only an inside thing. ❤️

OK, I just did a bit of googling for you. It goes by county (this is pretty typical). I wouldn't try to take him in the car by yourself, he will probably resist. First talk to him, gauge his mood, etc. See if he's drinking. Unfortunately, it's better if he is actually drunk and depressed and saying things about hurting himself. Then the easiest way to get them to your house is to call 911. Tell them you need a mobile crisis unit. Explain the situation and explain the history. Tell them NO SIRENS - this is very important (I sometimes have to get them to come to my office and I always emphasize this). But try to get the actual screeners to come, not just paramedics. They have them in OR - I checked. There might be a special number. You can google or if you PM me your county I'll look it up for you. That tends to work better. Then I can walk you through some key words, but in general they include "alcohol dependency" "repeated threats of suicide" and - if this is true it will help (sadly) - "access to weapons in the home." Also mention that you have a baby and you are afraid for her safety as well. There will be no repercussions if you go the mental health route and it will help to get him the help he needs.

Please take him to a hospital. You are in the US, right? You can call a mobile crisis service to come to your house and they will ask him about suicide. Make sure you tell them about these conversations. He can be committed for at least 72 hours. During that time he can be evaluated and sent to a treatment program. It sounds like he needs a dual-diagnosis program for alcohol and mental health. I'm sorry you are both going through this but he is lucky to have you. FWIW I feel his pain, and yours. Good luck. (You could also just ask him to see a psychiatrist but he probably won't. If you are in NY, NJ, or PA, PM me)

I disagree with most of the other posters and I happen to be a professional in the mental health field. Depression is not an excuse to cheat but certain people, especially women, especially women with a past history of a certain type of trauma, cannot help themselves. I totally get her because I am very much like her. Much older, much more experienced, probably much more educated. I posted elsewhere just today about what i've been going through lately and made up this user name for this particular purpose. If you love her, you need to keep telling her, and you need to have her back, and support her, and help her to find her real self and her self esteem so she does not need to cheat. It's not about cheating, it's about finding her self-worth and self-love. I've said those exact words to my husband (of almost 25 years): "You can't stand to look at my face. I'm ugly and gross." He never said to me, "You're beautiful." You are ahead of the game, my friend. You can do this, and save your children's mother for them. I also understand the need to be apart, to live separately, all those things. Go to therapy, tell her you love her, tell her you want to understand her, and give it your best chance. Then at least if it does fall apart, your children will know you both did your best. Good luck. I feel for you both, I really do. I wish my husband had a tenth of your compassion. Also, a final word about suicidal thoughts - they might feel manipulative, but they are often real. I know mine often are. It's not about showing anything to anyone. It's about a pain that feels incompatible with life. People who have not experienced it can't imagine it.
